cover.title: Project Lighthouse
cover.subtitle: A demo-ready car-wash CDD on the aqmen platform, built end to end in two weeks
cover.summary: A two-week sprint (12 to 23 October 2026) in which the delivery team runs the Spanish car-wash case through every step of an aqmen project, from the brief to the deck, so sales can demo a finished workspace whose every number traces to a source.
footer_lines: Aqmen AI Limited · Company No. 16117654 · Camburgh House, 27 New Dover Road, Canterbury, Kent CT1 3DN · aqmen.ai

blocks.text: Prospects ask to see a finished diligence, not a blank workspace. Today each demo is assembled by hand from slides, and the numbers on screen cannot be traced back to the data that produced them.

items: **Whether the car-wash case becomes the standard demo** for CDD prospects from November.
**Which gaps in the platform block a client-grade readout,** ranked for the next product cycle.
**Time pressure:** three prospect demos are booked for the first week of November.
**Q1.** Can one workspace carry a CDD from brief to deck with every figure cited?
**Q2.** How long does each step take with the agents, and where does a person still decide?
**Q3.** Which platform gaps would a client notice in a live demo?

sections.heading: 2 · Our approach: two workstreams, one per week

items.text: Public data supports a bottom-up market size within 20% of the trade association's figure.
The full flow runs in under five working days once the brief is agreed.
The deliverable skills render the deck from the workspace without manual edits to numbers.

items: **Scope and research.** Brief written to the workspace; parallel researchers load the car parc, station census and survey data as cited datasets.
**Model and challenge.** Driver tree from cars to spend, then the structure and values critics, with every finding triaged.
A validated Base model, insights per question, and a log of time spent per step.
**Conclude and deliver.** A view per question, then the deck, report and summary from one content file.
**Dry-run the demo.** Two rehearsals with sales; every gap a viewer notices goes on the list with its severity.
The demo deck and run-of-show, and a ranked platform gap list. Verdict on each hypothesis, with the evidence.

rows: The car-wash project on the platform: cited datasets, the model, insights and a view per question. Nothing stale at handover.
Rendered from the workspace; every number traced to a dataset.
Question by question: the figure to show, the chart or view to open, the fallback.
Each gap with what a viewer saw, its severity and a proposed fix, ranked for the product cycle.

items: Fixing the gaps found; they feed the next product cycle.

blocks.text: The sprint starts on Monday 12 October and closes on Friday 23 October. A fifteen-minute stand-up each morning; findings on Fridays, prepared backwards from the storyline.

rows: Brief agreed; questions and hypotheses fixed
Base model and critic findings; go or no-go on the readout
Final run-through; gap list handed to product
Sprint lead: the storyline, the readout and the demo rehearsals
Platform lead: triages every gap the sprint finds
Runs the flow with the agents and logs time per step

items: **One channel.** The sprint thread; decisions logged in the workspace brief.
